title: Wheelchair accessible taxis
excerpt: Ramp and hoist wheelchair taxis across the Peninsula and Frankston, with door-to-door help, 24/7.
description: Wheelchair accessible taxi on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston. Ramp van or hoist Maxi, four-point restraints, carers welcome, 24/7.

content.p: A wheelchair accessible taxi should feel like any other taxi ride: you book it, it turns up, and you get where you are going without fuss. At Taxi Peninsula, accessible travel is a large part of what we do every day, from short hops around Mornington and Rosebud to longer trips across Frankston and into Melbourne. You stay seated in your own chair for the whole journey, and the driver handles the ramp or hoist, the restraints and the door-to-door help.

content.h2: Which vehicle is right for me?

content.p: We run two kinds of wheelchair accessible vehicle, and the booking form helps you choose. If you are not sure, tell us about the chair and who is travelling and we will suggest the better fit.

ul: Wheelchair accessible van: a rear ramp, room for one wheelchair plus four seated passengers. It suits most manual chairs and many lighter power chairs.

Maxi WAT: a hydraulic hoist rather than a ramp, room for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. It is the right choice for heavier power chairs, larger tilt-in-space chairs or two wheelchair users travelling together.
Sedan: a standard taxi for passengers who can transfer into a car seat, with a folding chair or walker stowed in the boot.

content.p: Every wheelchair vehicle has four-point wheelchair restraints, a lap-sash seatbelt for the passenger and air-conditioning, which matters on a hot Peninsula afternoon.

content.h2: How the trip works from your door

content.p: Your driver comes to the door rather than waiting at the kerb. They will help you down a step or along a driveway if needed, position the chair on the ramp or hoist platform, and secure it with all four restraints before fitting your seatbelt. Brakes are checked, footplates are clear, and you are asked whether you are comfortable before the vehicle moves.

At the other end the process runs in reverse. The driver lowers you to ground level, releases the restraints and walks with you to the entrance, whether that is a clinic reception in Frankston, a café in Sorrento or a family home in Hastings. If you need a moment to settle, there is no rush.

A carer travels with the passenger, and in the larger vehicles there is room for family as well. This makes the Maxi useful for outings where a wheelchair user and several relatives want to arrive together, rather than splitting across two cars. Let us know how many people are coming so we send a vehicle with enough seats.

content.h2: Paying with MPTP, NDIS or aged-care funding

content.p: We accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program (MPTP) cards, and we can bill approved NDIS and aged-care accounts. Bring your MPTP card on the day and the driver will process it at the end of the trip. For NDIS and aged-care travel, mention the arrangement when you book so the paperwork is right from the start. A fare estimate appears on the booking form, and if you need a firm figure for a plan manager or support coordinator, ask us for a fixed quote.

content.h2: Booking a wheelchair taxi on the Peninsula

content.p: We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, but accessible vehicles are in demand, so booking ahead is recommended, especially for early-morning appointments or weekend outings. The online form takes about two minutes, or you can phone us. You will receive confirmation by SMS or email.

When you book, a few details help us get it right first time: the type and approximate size of the chair, whether it is manual or powered, any steps at the pick-up address, and anything the driver should know about getting in or out. We cover the whole Mornington Peninsula, Frankston and south-east Melbourne, and we travel anywhere in Melbourne, so a trip from Rye to a specialist in the city, or from Frankston to a sporting event, is no problem.

Regular trips are welcome too. Many passengers book the same day and time each week for dialysis, physiotherapy, day programs or shopping, and having the booking set up in advance means one less thing to organise.

expect: Driver comes to your door and helps with steps or driveways
Chair secured with four-point restraints, plus your own lap-sash seatbelt
Air-conditioned van or Maxi, matched to your chair and group
MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts accepted

faq.q: Can I stay in my wheelchair for the whole trip?
faq.a: Yes. In both the wheelchair accessible van and the Maxi WAT you remain seated in your own chair. The driver secures it with four-point restraints and fits a lap-sash seatbelt for you. If you prefer to transfer to a seat and travel in a sedan, that is also possible, and a folding chair can go in the boot.

faq.q: My power chair is quite heavy. Which vehicle should I book?
faq.a: Book the Maxi WAT. It uses a hydraulic hoist rather than a ramp, which makes it the better choice for heavier power chairs and larger tilt-in-space models. If you are unsure, describe the chair when you book or phone us, and we will confirm which vehicle suits it before the day.

faq.q: Can my carer and family come with me?
faq.a: A carer travels with the passenger. The van seats four passengers as well as the wheelchair user, and the Maxi seats six alongside two wheelchairs, so family members can usually come too. Tell us the total number of people when booking so we allocate a vehicle with enough room for everyone.

faq.q: Do you accept MPTP cards?
faq.a: Yes, we accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards. Have your card with you and the driver will process it at the end of the trip. We also bill approved NDIS and aged-care accounts. Mention how you are paying when you book so the right details are ready before your driver arrives.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book a wheelchair taxi?
faq.a: We run around the clock, but accessible vehicles are popular, so book as early as you can, particularly for early appointments, weekends and public holidays. The online form takes about two minutes and you will receive an SMS or email confirmation. Same-day requests are worth trying too, so call us if plans change.

title: Medical & hospital trips
excerpt: Reliable taxis to appointments, day procedures and hospital discharge, with pick up when you are ready.
description: Taxi to Frankston Hospital, Rosebud Hospital and Melbourne specialists from the Mornington Peninsula. Door-to-door help and pick up when ready.

content.p: Getting to a medical appointment is stressful enough without worrying about parking, buses or asking a neighbour for a lift. Taxi Peninsula takes people from homes across the Mornington Peninsula and Frankston to GP clinics, specialists, imaging centres, dialysis units and hospitals, then brings them home again. You can travel in a standard sedan or a wheelchair accessible vehicle, and the driver helps from door to door.
Most of our medical trips are local, but we travel anywhere in Melbourne when treatment takes you further afield. Common destinations include:

ul: Frankston Hospital and Rosebud Hospital, the public hospitals run by Peninsula Health
Peninsula Private Hospital and local day surgery centres
GP clinics, physiotherapists, dentists and pathology collection centres around Mornington, Hastings, Somerville and the southern Peninsula
Monash Medical Centre in Clayton and specialist hospitals in the city, such as The Alfred and the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre
Regular dialysis, chemotherapy and rehabilitation sessions

content.p: Large hospitals have several entrances and departments spread across a big site. Tell us the department or clinic when you book and the driver will aim for the closest drop-off point, then help you to the door.

content.h2: Hospital discharge with “pick up when ready”

content.p: Discharge times are notoriously hard to predict. Paperwork, pharmacy and a final check from the doctor can stretch a morning into an afternoon. Our “pick up when ready” option is designed for this. Book the trip in advance without a fixed time, then tap “I’m ready” on your booking or give us a call when you are cleared to leave. We dispatch a vehicle at that point, so nobody has to guess a time in advance, and you are not stuck in a waiting room hoping one is free.
Family members can make the booking on a patient’s behalf, which is helpful when someone is coming home after surgery and should not be handling their phone or luggage.

The same option works for appointments that are hard to time, such as scans, infusions or a long wait in an outpatient clinic. You get to the appointment on a fixed booking, then let us know when you are finished for the trip home.

Not every hospital trip is for the patient. We also take partners, parents and friends to visit people in Frankston Hospital, Rosebud Hospital or one of the big Melbourne hospitals, including late in the evening when buses are infrequent. For older visitors who find hospital car parks tiring to navigate, being dropped near the entrance and collected from the same spot can make visiting much easier. If you would like to bring a few belongings for the patient, such as a bag of clothes or a walking frame, there is room in the boot.

After sedation or a day procedure, many clinics will not let you drive yourself home. A taxi is a sensible alternative, and our drivers understand that passengers may be tired, sore or a little unsteady. They will carry bags, open doors and take the trip at a calm pace. If you have mobility aids, crutches or a wheelchair, mention it when booking so the right vehicle arrives.

content.h2: Wheelchair users and passengers with limited mobility

content.p: Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist suitable for heavier power chairs. Both use four-point wheelchair restraints and lap-sash seatbelts. A carer travels with the passenger, which is often important at appointments where someone needs to take notes or help with instructions.

We accept MPTP cards and can bill approved NDIS and aged-care accounts, which covers a large share of medical travel for our regular passengers. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and fixed quotes are available on request if you need to plan around a budget. Bookings are recommended, particularly for early appointments, and we operate 24 hours a day if you need to get to an emergency department or come home late at night.

expect: Help from your front door to the clinic or ward entrance
Pick up when ready for hospital discharge, no clock-watching
Sedan or wheelchair vehicle, with room for a carer
Confirmation by SMS or email when you book

faq.q: How does “pick up when ready” work?
faq.a: Book your trip home in advance and choose the pick up when ready option instead of a fixed time. When the hospital clears you to leave, tap “I’m ready” on your booking or phone us, and we send a vehicle then. It suits hospital discharge, day surgery and appointments that tend to run late.

faq.q: Can you drop me at a particular department?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us the department, clinic or ward when you book and the driver will head for the most suitable drop-off point at that hospital or medical centre. If the entrance is a short walk from where vehicles can stop, the driver will help you get there.

faq.q: Can someone else book a medical trip for me?
faq.a: Absolutely. Family members, carers, support coordinators and clinic staff often book for patients. Give us the passenger’s name, pick-up address and any mobility needs, and choose whether the confirmation goes to the passenger or the person booking. The driver will ask for the passenger by name on arrival.

faq.q: Do you go to hospitals in Melbourne as well as on the Peninsula?
faq.a: Yes. Alongside Frankston Hospital and Rosebud Hospital, we regularly take passengers to Monash Medical Centre in Clayton and specialist hospitals in the city. We travel anywhere in Melbourne, so you can book a return trip for treatment, follow-up appointments or visiting a relative in hospital.

faq.q: I need a regular trip for dialysis. Can I set that up?
faq.a: Yes. Many passengers have standing bookings for dialysis, chemotherapy or rehabilitation on the same days each week. Let us know the schedule, the treatment centre and whether you need a wheelchair vehicle. MPTP cards are accepted, and approved NDIS and aged-care accounts can be billed for these regular trips.

title: Airport transfers
excerpt: Taxi transfers to Melbourne, Avalon, Moorabbin and Essendon Fields airports, with flight tracking.
description: Airport taxi from the Mornington Peninsula and Frankston to Melbourne (Tullamarine), Avalon and more. Flight tracking and wheelchair vehicles.

content.p: An early flight from the Peninsula usually means a dark, quiet drive before dawn, and the last thing you want is to be wondering whether your taxi will show up. Taxi Peninsula runs airport transfers around the clock from Frankston, Mornington, Mount Martha, Dromana, Sorrento and every town in between. Book ahead, get a confirmation by SMS or email, and your driver will be there when you need to leave.

ul: Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine, for domestic and international flights
Avalon Airport, on the western side of Port Phillip near Geelong
Moorabbin Airport, used for charter, training and light aircraft flights
Essendon Fields, for private and charter departures

content.p: Melbourne Airport handles most of our airport work, but Avalon is worth considering when the fares or flight times suit you better. It sits on the far side of Port Phillip, so the drive takes you right around the bay, and we plan your pick-up time accordingly.

content.h2: Getting picked up when you land

content.p: Add your flight number to the booking and we track the flight. If you land early or late, we adjust the pick-up time to match, so you are not left waiting at the kerb wondering where your ride is. Once you have collected your bags, follow the airport signage to the taxi and pick-up areas, and keep your phone on in case your driver needs to reach you.
Coming home late at night after a long-haul flight is when a pre-booked taxi is most welcome. Instead of joining a queue, you know a car is coming to take you back to Frankston or down to Portsea.

A sedan is fine for one or two travellers with suitcases. For families, golf trips or groups heading away together, the Maxi WAT seats up to six passengers alongside two wheelchairs, so it handles a fuller load of people and bags in one vehicle. Tell us how many suitcases, prams or sports bags you have and we will suggest the right vehicle.

If you travel in a wheelchair, our wheelchair accessible van (rear ramp) and Maxi WAT (hydraulic hoist) let you stay in your own chair to the terminal. Each secures the chair with four-point restraints and gives you a lap-sash seatbelt. Airlines often ask wheelchair users to check in early to arrange assistance, so allow extra time when you choose your pick-up and we will plan around it. MPTP cards are accepted where eligible.

The online booking form takes about two minutes and shows a fare estimate before you confirm. If you prefer a set figure, perhaps for a business trip or a family holiday budget, ask us for a fixed quote. Book as far ahead as you can for early-morning departures and busy holiday periods, and include your flight number for any pick-up from the airport.
Hotel and resort guests on the Peninsula can book the same way, and we are happy to collect you from your accommodation rather than a home address.

A little preparation the night before makes an early start much easier. Have your bags packed and by the door, your passport or ID in your hand luggage, and the house keys sorted. If you live on a long rural driveway in Red Hill or Main Ridge, or in an apartment block in Frankston with a tricky entrance, add a note to your booking so the driver knows exactly where to stop. For groups, double-check that everyone is being collected from the same address, or list each stop if we are picking people up along the way.

International travellers should allow more time at the terminal than domestic passengers, and school holidays and long weekends tend to make airports busier. When choosing your pick-up time, think about check-in deadlines and security queues rather than just the flight time, and remember the drive from the southern Peninsula to Tullamarine crosses the whole of Melbourne. If you are not sure when to leave, ask us when you book and we will help you work out a sensible time.

expect: Flight tracking when you add your flight number
Available 24/7 for early departures and late arrivals
Sedan, accessible van or Maxi for luggage and groups
Fare estimate on booking; fixed quotes on request

faq.q: What happens if my flight is delayed?
faq.a: When you include your flight number in the booking, we track the flight and adjust your pick-up to the actual landing time. That way the driver is there when you come through, whether the plane is early or running late. If your flight is cancelled or diverted, call us and we will rearrange the booking.

faq.q: Can you take me to Avalon Airport from the Peninsula?
faq.a: Yes. We run transfers to Avalon as well as Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine, and to Moorabbin Airport and Essendon Fields for charter and private flights. Avalon is on the other side of the bay, so allow plenty of time when choosing your departure, and book early for morning flights.

faq.q: Where do I meet my driver at the airport?
faq.a: After you collect your luggage, follow the airport signage to the taxi and pick-up areas. Keep your phone switched on so your driver can contact you if needed. Arrangements differ between airports and terminals, so if you have any doubt, ask when you book and we will explain what to do.

faq.q: We are a family of five with lots of luggage. Will we fit?
faq.a: For larger families or groups, book the Maxi WAT, which seats up to six passengers and has more room than a sedan. Tell us how many suitcases, prams, car seats or sports bags you are bringing so we can confirm everything fits. If it will not, we can suggest a second vehicle.

faq.q: Can I get a fixed price for my airport transfer?
faq.a: The booking form shows a fare estimate before you confirm, which gives most travellers a good idea of the cost. If you need a set figure for budgeting or a business expense claim, ask us for a fixed quote when you book. We will confirm the details by SMS or email.

title: NDIS & aged care
excerpt: Taxi travel for NDIS participants and aged-care clients, with account billing and carers welcome.
description: NDIS and aged care taxi transport on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston. Account billing, MPTP cards, wheelchair vehicles and carers welcome.

content.p: Transport is often what makes the rest of a support plan possible. Getting to work, a day program, therapy, the shops or a friend’s place depends on having a ride you can count on. Taxi Peninsula provides regular and one-off trips for NDIS participants and people receiving aged-care services across the Mornington Peninsula, Frankston and south-east Melbourne, in standard sedans and wheelchair accessible vehicles.

We take bookings directly from participants and older clients, and from the people who help them: family members, support coordinators, plan managers, support workers and aged-care providers. Whoever arranges the trip, the passenger gets the same calm, patient service and help from door to door.

We accept approved NDIS and aged-care accounts, so trips can be billed rather than paid on the day where that arrangement is in place. We also accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program (MPTP) cards. When you first book, tell us how the trip is funded and who should receive invoices or trip details, and we will set it up so future bookings run smoothly.

Plan managers and coordinators sometimes need a figure before approving travel. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and we can provide a fixed quote on request for a particular trip or a regular run.

ul: Day programs, community groups and social outings
Work, volunteering, TAFE and study
Therapy and allied health: physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech, hydrotherapy
GP visits, specialists and hospital appointments
Shopping at Bayside Shopping Centre, Mornington, Rosebud or your local centre
Visiting family, church, clubs and weekend activities

content.p: Many of our NDIS and aged-care passengers travel at the same time each week, and routine matters. Standing bookings mean you do not have to organise every trip from scratch, and you know what to expect. Drivers walk passengers to and from the door, help with shopping bags and walking frames, and take the time to make sure seatbelts are fastened and everyone is settled.

For wheelchair users, our van has a rear ramp for one wheelchair and four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs and six seated passengers, which suits heavier power chairs. Every wheelchair vehicle has four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning.

content.h2: Support workers and carers travelling along

content.p: Carers are welcome on board with the passenger. That might be a support worker heading to a community access shift, a family member coming to an appointment, or a staff member from a residential aged-care home. Let us know how many people are travelling so the right vehicle is sent.

Group outings from a day program or residential home are easier in the Maxi WAT, which can carry two wheelchair users and six seated passengers together. That makes a trip to the foreshore at Mornington, a lunch in Rosebud or a visit to Arthurs Seat a single booking instead of several cars.

Some passengers find travel with an unfamiliar driver unsettling, particularly people living with dementia, autism, anxiety or a recent brain injury. Small details help, and we are glad to hear them when you book: a preferred seat, whether the passenger likes to chat or would rather ride quietly, whether someone needs to meet them at the destination, and who to call if anything is unclear. If a passenger needs supervision, tell us who will meet them at the other end so the driver can walk them to that person rather than leaving them at the door.

For aged-care clients living at home, a reliable taxi can be the difference between staying connected and becoming isolated. A regular lift to the bowls club, a weekly hairdresser appointment or Sunday lunch with family is just as worthwhile as a medical trip, and we treat it that way.

We run 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and bookings are recommended so we can plan vehicles, particularly for accessible trips. Book online in about two minutes or phone us, and confirmations are sent by SMS or email to whoever you nominate.

expect: Approved NDIS and aged-care accounts billed, MPTP cards accepted
Carers and support workers travel with the passenger
Standing bookings for weekly programs and therapy
Confirmations sent to the participant, family or coordinator

faq.q: Can my NDIS plan pay for the taxi?
faq.a: We bill approved NDIS accounts, so if your plan includes transport funding and the arrangement is in place, trips can be invoiced rather than paid on the day. Talk to your plan manager or support coordinator about what your plan covers, then tell us how you would like billing handled when you first book.

faq.q: Do you provide transport for aged-care clients?
faq.a: Yes. We bill approved aged-care accounts and regularly carry older passengers to appointments, shopping, social groups and family visits. Drivers help from door to door and are used to walking frames, folding wheelchairs and passengers who need a little extra time. Residential care staff and family members can book on a client’s behalf.

faq.q: Can a support coordinator book on my behalf?
faq.a: Yes. Support coordinators, plan managers, support workers and family members all make bookings for passengers. Give us the passenger’s details, any mobility needs and who should receive confirmations, and we will keep that information with future trips. The driver will always ask for the passenger by name on pick-up.

faq.q: Can I set up a regular weekly booking?
faq.a: Yes, and many passengers prefer it. Tell us the days, times and addresses for your regular trips, whether to a day program, therapy, work or shopping, and we will set them up. If something changes, such as a cancelled session or a public holiday, just let us know and we adjust the booking.

faq.q: Does my support worker pay a separate fare?
faq.a: A carer or support worker travels with the passenger as part of the same trip. If you are unsure how this applies under your particular funding arrangement, mention it when you book and check with your plan manager, and we will make sure the trip details are recorded clearly for billing.

title: Group & Maxi travel
excerpt: Maxi taxi travel for small groups, families and mixed groups with wheelchair users, in one vehicle.
description: Maxi taxi for groups on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston. Six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, hoist access and air-conditioning.

content.p: Some trips just work better when everyone travels together. A family heading to the airport, friends going out for dinner in Mornington, colleagues travelling to a conference in the city or a day program outing with two wheelchair users all share the same problem: one sedan is not enough. Taxi Peninsula’s Maxi WAT solves that by carrying up to six seated passengers and two wheelchairs in a single air-conditioned vehicle.

WAT stands for wheelchair accessible taxi. Our Maxi WAT is a larger vehicle with a hydraulic hoist at the rear, so it can lift wheelchairs, including heavier power chairs, smoothly up to floor level. Inside, wheelchair positions have four-point restraints and every passenger has a lap-sash seatbelt. When no wheelchairs are travelling, the Maxi is simply a roomy taxi for a group.

Because it is both a group vehicle and an accessible vehicle, the Maxi is ideal for mixed groups. A grandparent in a wheelchair does not need to travel separately from the rest of the family, and two friends who both use chairs can go to the same concert in the same vehicle.

ul: Family trips to Melbourne Airport or Avalon with several suitcases
Nights out in Frankston, Mornington or Sorrento, with everyone dropped home afterwards
Weddings, birthdays and celebrations where guests want to arrive together
Footy at the MCG or Marvel Stadium, concerts and race days
Winery and day trips around Red Hill, Main Ridge and the southern Peninsula
Day program, school and aged-care outings that include wheelchair users

content.p: Good group bookings start with good information. When you book, tell us the total number of passengers, how many are in wheelchairs and what kind of chairs they use, and roughly how much luggage or equipment is coming. If people are being collected from different addresses, list each stop in order. For drop-offs at the end of a night out, give us everyone’s home suburb so we can plan a sensible route.

The Maxi seats six passengers plus two wheelchair users. If your group is larger than that, we can send more than one vehicle, for example a Maxi with a sedan or a second accessible van, and coordinate them so everyone arrives at about the same time. Ask about this when you book so we can check what is available.

content.h2: Splitting the cost and getting a quote

content.p: Travelling as a group in one vehicle is often more practical than organising several cars, and it means nobody has to be the sober driver. The booking form shows a fare estimate for the trip, and if you want a set figure to share among the group, ask us for a fixed quote. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers, and approved NDIS and aged-care accounts can be billed for group outings where that applies.

content.h2: Booking a Maxi on the Peninsula

content.p: Maxi vehicles are in high demand on Friday and Saturday nights, on public holidays and during the summer holiday season on the Peninsula, when visitors fill towns from Mount Martha to Portsea. Book as early as you can for those times. We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, the online booking takes about two minutes, and you will get confirmation by SMS or email.

For regular group runs, such as a weekly social club trip or a sporting team heading to away games, we can set up a standing booking so the same vehicle type is reserved each time. Let us know the pattern and we will take it from there.

Whatever the occasion, your driver helps everyone on and off, operates the hoist for wheelchair users and makes sure the whole group is buckled in before setting off. If someone in the group needs a little more time or a steadying hand on the step, the driver will take it slowly, and bags, walking frames and folded prams are loaded for you. At the end of the trip, nobody is left on a dark street wondering how to cover the last stretch home.

expect: Up to six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs
Hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs, with four-point restraints
Multiple pick-ups and drop-offs planned in one booking
Extra vehicles coordinated for groups larger than one Maxi

faq.q: How many people fit in a Maxi taxi?
faq.a: Our Maxi WAT carries up to six seated passengers plus two wheelchair users. Every passenger has a lap-sash seatbelt, and wheelchairs are secured with four-point restraints. If your group is bigger than one Maxi, we can send an additional vehicle and coordinate both so the group travels at about the same time.

faq.q: Can the Maxi pick people up from different addresses?
faq.a: Yes. List each pick-up address in order when you book, and the driver will collect everyone along the way. The same works in reverse at the end of a night out, with passengers dropped at their own homes. Giving us all the addresses upfront lets us plan the most sensible route.

faq.q: Is the Maxi only for wheelchair users?
faq.a: No. The Maxi is a wheelchair accessible taxi, but it is just as useful for groups without any wheelchairs. Families, friends, work teams and sporting groups book it for airport trips, dinners, events and day trips simply because everyone can travel in one vehicle together.

faq.q: Will our luggage fit for an airport trip?
faq.a: Tell us how many suitcases, prams, golf bags or other large items you have when you book. We will confirm whether everything fits in the Maxi with your group, or suggest a second vehicle if needed. Space depends on how many seats and wheelchair positions are in use on the trip.

faq.q: How far ahead should we book a Maxi?
faq.a: As early as possible, especially for weekend nights, public holidays, the summer season on the Peninsula and big event days in Melbourne. Maxi vehicles are popular with groups and wheelchair users alike. Book online in about two minutes or phone us, and you will receive an SMS or email confirmation.

title: Events & day trips
excerpt: Taxis to the footy, concerts, races and weddings, plus relaxed day trips around the Peninsula.
description: Event taxi from the Mornington Peninsula and Frankston to the footy, concerts and races, plus day trips. Sedans, wheelchair vans and Maxi taxis.

content.p: Big days out are more enjoyable when you are not watching the clock for the last train or worrying about parking near a stadium. Taxi Peninsula takes people from Frankston and the Mornington Peninsula to events across Melbourne and brings them home again, and we run relaxed day trips around the Peninsula for locals and visitors alike. Choose a sedan for a couple of people, a wheelchair accessible van, or a Maxi for a group.

Getting from the Peninsula to the MCG or Marvel Stadium on a game day can be a long journey by public transport, especially for older fans or anyone using a wheelchair. A pre-booked taxi drops you as close as traffic arrangements allow and collects you after the final siren. Crowds and road closures around the stadiums can make pick-ups slower, so agree a meeting point with your driver and keep your phone on.

We take concert-goers to Rod Laver Arena, Margaret Court Arena and the theatres in the city, and to performances closer to home such as shows at the Frankston Arts Centre. Late finishes are no problem because we operate 24 hours a day. For wheelchair users with accessible seating booked, our ramp van and hoist-equipped Maxi make getting there straightforward, with a carer or friend travelling alongside.

Race days are social occasions, and nobody wants to be the designated driver. We run passengers to Flemington and Caulfield for the big Melbourne meetings, and to local tracks including Mornington Racecourse and Cranbourne. Groups of up to six, or two wheelchair users with six seated passengers, can travel together in the Maxi. On major carnival days traffic around the tracks is heavy, so book early and allow extra time.

Weddings, milestone birthdays, anniversary lunches and work functions often involve guests coming from different places and leaving at different times. We can run guests between a ceremony and reception, take older relatives home early, and collect the late-night crowd at the end. For a full wedding plan, see our dedicated weddings page.
The Peninsula is made for slow days out, and a taxi lets everyone enjoy the scenery rather than the road. Popular ideas include:

ul: The bayside towns of Mornington, Mount Martha, Dromana, Rosebud and Sorrento
Point Nepean National Park and the historic Quarantine Station area near Portsea
Arthurs Seat for the views over Port Phillip
Peninsula Hot Springs at Fingal
Cellar doors and farm gates around Red Hill, Main Ridge and Merricks
Coastal walks and beaches along the back beaches and Western Port

content.p: We can design a simple plan with you: where to start, where to stop for lunch and when to head home. Tell us if anyone in the group uses a wheelchair or walking frame, so we can choose stops with easy access and send a suitable vehicle.

Event traffic is unpredictable, so build in a buffer. Book your pick-up earlier than you think you need, especially for a bounce-down, a first race or a concert with a strict door time. Take a note of the meeting point you agreed with the driver, and if you are in a group, make sure everyone knows it too. If the event finishes early or goes into extra time, a quick call lets us move your pick-up. For wheelchair users, check the venue’s accessible drop-off arrangements before the day and tell us what you find, so the driver heads straight to the right spot. A charged phone and a little patience go a long way on the busiest nights of the year.

For visiting relatives, a day trip is a good way to see the Peninsula without anyone having to drive. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and fixed quotes are available on request for planned outings. Booking takes about two minutes online, or call if you would rather talk it through; we confirm everything by SMS or email.

expect: Return trips planned around event start and finish times
Pre-arranged meeting points for crowded stadium pick-ups
Group Maxi or accessible vehicle, depending on who is coming
Day trips shaped around your stops and pace

faq.q: Can you pick us up after the game or concert?
faq.a: Yes. Book a return trip and agree a meeting point near the venue when you book. Crowds and road closures can make stadium and arena pick-ups slow, so keep your phone switched on and let the driver know when you are leaving. If the event runs late, call us and we will adjust the pick-up.

faq.q: Do you go to the races at Flemington and Caulfield?
faq.a: Yes. We take passengers from the Peninsula and Frankston to Flemington and Caulfield, as well as to Mornington Racecourse and Cranbourne. Big race days bring heavy traffic and busy drop-off areas, so book well ahead and allow extra time. Groups can travel together in the Maxi.

faq.q: Can a wheelchair user come to an event with friends?
faq.a: Yes. Our wheelchair accessible van carries one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. Both have four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts, so a wheelchair user can travel in the same vehicle as friends or family to the game, concert or show.

faq.q: Can you plan a day trip around the Peninsula for us?
faq.a: We can help you shape a simple day out, such as a drive along the bay to Sorrento, lunch in Red Hill and a stop at Arthurs Seat. Tell us what interests your group, any mobility needs and how long you want to be out, and we will suggest a plan and a suitable vehicle.

faq.q: How do we book an event trip?
faq.a: Use the online form, which takes about two minutes, or ring us with the event, the venue, the number of passengers and when you want collecting afterwards. An SMS or email confirms the booking. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and we can provide a fixed quote on request for planned outings.

title: Local taxi service
excerpt: Everyday taxi rides around the Peninsula and Frankston, day or night: shops, station, dinner and home.
description: Local taxi on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston, 24/7. Rides to the shops, the station, dinner and home again, booked online in minutes.

content.p: Not every trip needs planning weeks in advance. Most of our work is ordinary, everyday travel: a ride to the supermarket, a lift to Frankston station, dinner in Main Street Mornington or getting home safely after a night out. Taxi Peninsula provides a local taxi service across the Mornington Peninsula and Frankston, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, in a comfortable sedan or, when you need it, a wheelchair accessible vehicle.

Our everyday trips cover the whole Peninsula, from Seaford and Carrum Downs in the north to Portsea and Flinders in the south, and across to Hastings and the Western Port side. Some of the most common runs are:

ul: Shopping at Bayside Shopping Centre in Frankston, Karingal Hub, Mornington, Rosebud or your local village
Frankston station, and the Stony Point line stations such as Hastings and Baxter
Restaurants and pubs in Mornington, Sorrento, Red Hill and Frankston
Work, school pick-ups and after-hours shifts
Hairdressers, gyms, banks, the post office and other quick errands
The Searoad ferry terminal at Sorrento

content.p: For most everyday travel, our sedan is the right choice: a normal taxi for one to four passengers and their shopping or overnight bags. Drivers help with heavier bags at the door, and if you use a walker or folding wheelchair and can transfer into a car seat, it can go in the boot. If you need to stay seated in your wheelchair, choose our ramp van or the Maxi WAT instead; the booking form shows the options clearly.

Public transport on the Peninsula thins out at night, and some towns have no train line at all. That makes a taxi the practical way home after dinner with friends, a birthday at the pub or a late shift. We run all night, every night, so a 2am ride from Frankston to Mount Eliza or a 5am start to get to work is just as possible as an afternoon trip to the shops. If you know you will need a ride home later, booking it in advance saves waiting at the end of the night.

The quickest way is to book online, which takes about two minutes. Enter your pick-up and destination, choose a vehicle and a time, and the form shows a fare estimate before you confirm. You can also phone us if you prefer to talk to someone. Either way, confirmation arrives by SMS or email.

Bookings are recommended, especially for busy times such as Friday and Saturday evenings, school holidays and summer weekends when the southern Peninsula fills with visitors. If you need a car soon, it is still worth trying; we will tell you honestly when we can be there. If we cannot reach you as quickly as you need, we would rather say so upfront than leave you guessing.

content.h2: Small things that make a difference

content.p: Local trips are often the ones that matter most day to day, so the details count. Add a note to your booking if your house is hard to find, if you will be waiting inside a shop rather than at the kerb, or if you are carrying something bulky. Regular passengers sometimes set up a standing booking, such as the same shopping trip every Thursday morning, so they never have to remember to call. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers on everyday trips too, not just medical ones.

Visitors are welcome as well. If you are staying in a holiday house in Rye or Blairgowrie, or with family in Somerville or Tyabb, a local taxi is an easy way to get around without hiring a car. You might use us for a morning at the Sorrento shops, a lift to a dinner booking in Red Hill, or a ride back from the beach with the kids and their gear. Tell us where you are staying and where you want to go, and we will look after the rest.

expect: Sedan taxis around the clock, every day of the year
Fare estimate shown before you confirm the booking
Help with shopping bags and luggage at the door
Wheelchair vehicles available when you need one

faq.q: Do you really operate 24 hours a day?
faq.a: Yes. Taxi Peninsula runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including late nights and early mornings. Bookings are recommended, especially for busy weekend evenings and early starts, so we can have a car ready. Book online in about two minutes or phone us, and you will receive confirmation by SMS or email.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi to Frankston station?
faq.a: Yes, Frankston station is one of our most common local destinations, along with stations on the Stony Point line such as Baxter and Hastings. Tell us your train time when you book so we can plan the pick-up, and allow a little extra time in peak periods when traffic around Frankston is heavier.

faq.q: Can I book a ride home in advance?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a good idea after dinner, a party or a night out. Book the trip home for the time you expect to leave and add any notes about where to meet. If your plans change, call us and we will adjust the time. It saves waiting around at the end of the night.

faq.q: How do I know what my local trip will cost?
faq.a: When you book online, the form shows a fare estimate for your trip before you confirm. That gives you a good idea of the cost before you travel. If you need a set figure, for example for a regular work trip, ask us for a fixed quote and we will confirm it with you.

faq.q: Can I use my MPTP card for everyday trips?
faq.a: Yes. Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards are accepted on our everyday local trips as well as medical travel, for eligible passengers. Just show your card to the driver when the trip ends. Wheelchair users can also book our ramp van or Maxi WAT for local rides.

title: Winery tours
excerpt: Day hire for Mornington Peninsula cellar doors, with a designated driver and room for groups.
description: Winery tour taxi on the Mornington Peninsula. A designated driver for cellar doors in Red Hill, Main Ridge and Merricks, with room for groups.

content.p: The Mornington Peninsula is a well-known cool-climate wine region, with cellar doors scattered through rolling hills and winding back roads. It is lovely country to explore, and it is also country where someone has to stay sober behind the wheel. With Taxi Peninsula, that someone is our driver. We take couples, friends and family groups on relaxed winery days, so everyone can enjoy the tastings and the views.

Rather than a fixed tour, think of it as hiring a taxi and driver for part or all of the day. You choose the wineries, the lunch stop and the pace, and we drive you between them, wait or return as arranged, and bring everyone home at the end. Tell us roughly how long you want to be out and which areas interest you, and we will help you put together a sensible route. The booking form gives a fare estimate, and for a planned day we can provide a fixed quote on request.
Most cellar doors sit in a handful of areas, each with its own character:

ul: Red Hill and Red Hill South, the heart of the region, with many cellar doors, restaurants and the local market
Main Ridge, higher and cooler, with small estates and farm gates along quiet roads
Merricks and Merricks North, rolling country running down towards Western Port
Moorooduc, closer to Mornington and Frankston, convenient for a shorter afternoon

content.p: Many wineries take bookings for tastings or lunch, and some have limited opening days, so we recommend checking with the cellar doors you want to visit and booking ahead, particularly on weekends and during the summer and Easter holidays. Let us know your reservations and we will build the timing around them.

For a birthday, a hens’ day or a long-planned catch-up with friends, the Maxi WAT carries up to six passengers in one vehicle, so the conversation keeps flowing between stops. Larger groups can book a second vehicle and we will coordinate the two. We can collect people from several homes, from a hotel or from Frankston station for friends coming down from Melbourne.

Winery country can be tricky for wheelchair users, with gravel car parks and sloping paths. Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and our Maxi WAT a hydraulic hoist, and both use four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts, so a wheelchair user can share the day with the rest of the group. Accessibility varies between cellar doors, so it is worth asking each winery about step-free entry and accessible toilets when you book your tastings. Our driver will drop you as close to the entrance as the property allows.

content.h2: Making the most of the day

content.p: Eat a proper breakfast, plan a long lunch, and leave room in the boot for the cases you will inevitably buy. Some visitors combine wineries with other Peninsula stops, such as a cheese or chocolate maker, a berry farm in season or a walk at Arthurs Seat. Others finish the afternoon with a soak at Peninsula Hot Springs in Fingal, or with dinner at a winery restaurant before the drive home. If you are staying at a hotel or resort, we can collect you from your door in the morning and drop you back in the evening, and the whole day runs on your timetable rather than a coach schedule.

A few practical points help the day go smoothly. Drink plenty of water between tastings, wear comfortable shoes for gravel paths and vineyard lawns, and bring a jacket, because the hills around Red Hill and Main Ridge can be noticeably cooler than the coast. Share your winery and lunch bookings with us beforehand, and nominate one person in the group as the contact for the driver, so changes to the plan are easy to pass on. If the group decides to linger longer over lunch, just let the driver know.

expect: A designated driver, so everyone in your group can enjoy tastings
Your choice of wineries, lunch stop and pace
Maxi for groups; ramp or hoist vehicles for wheelchair users
Fixed quote available for planned winery days

faq.q: Is this a set tour or can we choose the wineries?
faq.a: You choose. Our winery days work as a taxi and driver hired for the time you need, so you pick the cellar doors, the lunch spot and how long you stay at each. If you would like suggestions, tell us what kind of day you are after and we will help you plan a sensible route.

faq.q: How much does a winery day cost?
faq.a: The cost depends on how long you want the vehicle, the route and the type of vehicle. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and for a planned winery day we recommend asking for a fixed quote so the whole group knows the cost upfront. Contact us with your plans and we will confirm the details.

faq.q: Do we need to book the wineries ourselves?
faq.a: Yes, we recommend booking tastings and lunch directly with the wineries, especially on weekends and in the summer holidays. Some cellar doors have limited opening days or require reservations. Once you have your bookings, share the times with us and we will plan the pick-ups and transfers around them.

faq.q: Can someone in a wheelchair come on a winery day?
faq.a: Yes. Our ramp van and hoist-equipped Maxi WAT let a wheelchair user travel with the group, secured with four-point restraints. Access at the wineries themselves varies, with some gravel paths and steps, so check with each cellar door about step-free entry. Our driver will drop you as close as the property allows.

faq.q: Can you pick up guests from Melbourne or a hotel?
faq.a: Yes. We can collect your group from homes across the Peninsula and Frankston, from Frankston station, from a Peninsula hotel or resort, or from addresses in Melbourne. List each pick-up when you book, and at the end of the day we will drop everyone back where they need to go.

title: Hotel & resort transfers
excerpt: Taxis for Peninsula hotel and resort guests: airports, wineries, hot springs, golf and weddings.
description: Hotel and resort transfers on the Mornington Peninsula. Taxi for guests to the airport, wineries, hot springs, golf and weddings, 24/7.

content.p: Plenty of visitors arrive on the Mornington Peninsula without a car, or would simply rather not drive once they are here. Taxi Peninsula looks after guests staying at hotels, resorts, boutique accommodation and holiday rentals, taking them from the airport to their door and then wherever their stay leads: a cellar door lunch, an afternoon at the hot springs, a round of golf or a wedding down the road.

Most guests begin with an airport transfer. We collect from Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine and from Avalon, and with your flight number in the booking we track the flight and time the pick-up to your actual arrival. From there we drive you directly to your accommodation, whether that is a hotel in Frankston or Mornington, a resort near Cape Schanck or Fingal, a cottage in Red Hill or Flinders, or a holiday apartment in Sorrento. Guests arriving by train can be collected from Frankston station instead.

content.h2: Where guests go during their stay

ul: Cellar doors and restaurants around Red Hill, Main Ridge, Merricks and Moorooduc
Peninsula Hot Springs and other wellness retreats around Fingal
Golf courses around Cape Schanck, Fingal, Rosebud and Mornington
Weddings and functions at Peninsula wineries, estates and private venues
Beaches, walks and lookouts, from Point Nepean National Park to Arthurs Seat
Dinner in town and back again, without anyone needing to drive

content.p: Because we are a local business, our drivers know the Peninsula’s back roads and the way into rural properties that can be confusing for visitors relying on a phone map. If your venue has a long driveway or an unmarked entrance, a note in your booking helps.

Guests staying several nights sometimes book a series of trips at once: the airport run in, a winery day midweek, dinner in Sorrento on the Saturday and the early transfer out. Setting these up together means fewer phone calls during your break, and you can still change or cancel individual trips if plans shift. Families travelling with grandparents or friends meeting up from different cities find this especially helpful.

Golfers often travel with clubs and buggies, so tell us how many sets you are bringing and we will send a vehicle with enough room, using the Maxi for a full group. For a day at the hot springs, arrange your drop-off to suit your bathing session, and a return pick-up for when you expect to finish. Winery days are best planned as a longer booking with a designated driver, which you can read about on our winery tours page.

Guests who use a wheelchair can travel in our ramp van, which carries one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, or our Maxi WAT with a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. That means a wheelchair user can get from the airport to the resort, then out to dinner or a winery, without hunting for an accessible hire car. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible Victorian passengers.

content.h2: Information for hotel and resort staff

content.p: Reception and concierge teams are welcome to book on behalf of guests. Give us the guest’s name, the pick-up time and destination, and any luggage or mobility details, and choose whether the confirmation goes to the guest or to the front desk. For a guest leaving to catch a flight, we can suggest a sensible departure time based on the airport and the time of day.

We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, which suits late check-ins and very early checkouts. Bookings are recommended, especially in summer, over Easter and on wedding weekends when the Peninsula is busiest. The online form takes about two minutes and shows a fare estimate, and fixed quotes are available on request for planned transfers or multi-stop days.

A pre-booked taxi can take much of the stress out of a short break. Instead of studying bus timetables or debating who will drive home from dinner, you can simply enjoy where you are staying and let someone local handle the roads.

expect: Door-to-door pick-up from your hotel, resort or holiday rental
Airport pick-ups timed to your flight with tracking
Room for luggage, golf clubs and small groups
Front desk and concierge bookings welcome

faq.q: Can you collect me from the airport and take me to my resort?
faq.a: Yes. We collect guests from Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine and from Avalon, and drive them straight to their accommodation anywhere on the Peninsula. Add your flight number when you book so we can track the flight and adjust the pick-up if you land early or late. Confirmation arrives by SMS or email.

faq.q: Can the hotel reception book a taxi for me?
faq.a: Yes. Reception and concierge staff often book on behalf of guests. They just need your name, the pick-up time, the destination and any luggage or mobility details. The confirmation can be sent to you or to the front desk, whichever is easier, and the driver will ask for you by name.

faq.q: Can you take us to Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Yes. We drop guests at Peninsula Hot Springs in Fingal and collect them again afterwards. Book your bathing session with the hot springs first, then arrange your drop-off to suit and a pick-up for when you expect to finish. If you are running late, call us and we will adjust the time.

faq.q: We are bringing golf clubs. Will they fit?
faq.a: Tell us how many golfers and how many sets of clubs when you book. A sedan suits one or two players, and for a full group we can send the Maxi, which has more room for people and equipment. If the load is large, we may suggest a second vehicle so nothing has to be squeezed in.

faq.q: Do you have wheelchair accessible vehicles for hotel guests?
faq.a: Yes. Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and our Maxi WAT a hydraulic hoist, and both use four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts. Guests who use wheelchairs can travel from the airport to their accommodation and on to restaurants, wineries or events in the same comfortable vehicle.

title: Weddings
excerpt: Guest transport for Peninsula weddings: ceremony, reception and accommodation, with accessible vehicles.
description: Wedding taxi transport on the Mornington Peninsula. Guest shuttles between ceremony, reception and accommodation, with wheelchair accessible vehicles.

content.p: The Mornington Peninsula has become a favourite place to get married, with ceremonies among the vines, receptions in winery restaurants and celebrations at coastal venues and private properties. What many couples discover during planning is that getting guests between those places is harder than it looks. Venues are often spread out along rural roads, accommodation is scattered across several towns, and nobody wants a guest driving home after the speeches. Taxi Peninsula helps by moving guests and wedding parties safely through the day and night.

content.h2: How we help on the day

ul: Bringing guests from their accommodation to the ceremony
Shuttling guests between the ceremony and the reception venue
Taking older relatives or families with young children home earlier in the evening
Late-night runs back to hotels, holiday houses and homes at the end of the reception
Airport transfers for interstate and overseas guests arriving for the wedding
Getting members of the wedding party to photo locations or the venue

content.p: We supply taxis, not decorated wedding cars, so we are a practical partner for the guests rather than the bridal arrival. Many couples use a wedding car for themselves and us for everyone else.

content.h2: Looking after older and less mobile guests

content.p: Weddings bring together grandparents, great-aunts and friends who may not find a long day easy. A rural winery with gravel paths and a ceremony on a sloping lawn can be a challenge for someone using a walking frame or wheelchair. Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp for one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs and six seated passengers. Wheelchairs are held by four-point restraints and every guest wears a lap-sash belt. Drivers help guests from the vehicle to the door, and a family member or carer travels with them. Having an accessible vehicle on hand means a grandparent can arrive with the family, and leave when they are tired rather than when the last bus goes.

The earlier you talk to us, the better, because wedding season on the Peninsula overlaps with summer holidays and the busiest weekends of the year. To help us plan, gather the date and times for the ceremony, reception and finish; the addresses of each venue and the main accommodation; the approximate number of guests needing transport at each stage; and anyone needing a wheelchair vehicle or extra help. We can then suggest a plan using sedans, our accessible van and the Maxi, and provide a fixed quote on request so you know the cost before the day.

For larger guest numbers, we coordinate several vehicles running in rounds rather than one large coach. It is worth thinking about which guests need transport most, such as those staying further away or those who will not be driving, and planning around them.

Different couples handle this differently. Some cover all guest transport as part of the wedding budget, and a fixed quote makes that easy to plan. Others simply recommend us to guests, who then book and pay for their own trips using the online form, which shows a fare estimate and takes about two minutes. You can also combine the two, covering the shuttle between ceremony and reception while guests book their own trips home. Tell us which approach you prefer and we will set things up to suit.

Late finishes are no problem because we run 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Nominate a contact person, perhaps a groomsman, bridesmaid or the venue coordinator, who can call us if timings change, so the couple are not answering phones during their own celebration. Guests who are leaving can be collected from the venue entrance, and our drivers will make sure everyone gets back to their bed safely, whether that is a hotel in Mornington or a holiday house in Rye. The morning after, we can also help guests get back to the venue to collect cars they sensibly left behind, or take interstate visitors to the airport for their flights home.

expect: Guest shuttles between accommodation, ceremony and reception
Accessible vehicles for older guests and wheelchair users
Late-night returns after the reception, 24/7
Fixed quotes on request for planned wedding transport

faq.q: Do you provide wedding cars for the couple?
faq.a: We provide taxis for guests and wedding parties, not decorated wedding cars. Many couples hire a special car for their own arrival and use us to move everyone else between accommodation, the ceremony and the reception. Our sedans, accessible van and Maxi can be combined to suit the size of your guest list.

faq.q: Can you shuttle guests between the ceremony and the reception?
faq.a: Yes. Give us the times and addresses of both venues and the number of guests needing transport, and we will plan vehicles to run between them, in several rounds if needed. Book well ahead, because wedding dates on the Peninsula often coincide with busy summer weekends and holiday periods.

faq.q: Some of our guests are elderly or use wheelchairs. Can you help?
faq.a: Yes, this is something we do well. Our ramp van and hoist-equipped Maxi WAT let wheelchair users stay in their own chairs, secured with four-point restraints, and drivers help less mobile guests to and from the door. These guests can then come and go when they are ready rather than at fixed times.

faq.q: Can guests book and pay for their own taxis?
faq.a: Yes. Some couples simply recommend us, and guests book their own trips online in about two minutes, with a fare estimate shown before they confirm. Others cover the transport themselves using a fixed quote. You can also mix the two, such as paying for the main shuttle while guests arrange their own trips home.

faq.q: How far in advance should we book wedding transport?
faq.a: As soon as you have your date and venues. Peninsula wedding season overlaps with summer holidays and long weekends, when vehicles, especially accessible ones and the Maxi, are in high demand. Early planning lets us map out the day and provide a fixed quote on request so you can include it in your budget.

title: Parcel delivery
excerpt: Same-day local delivery of parcels, documents and keys by taxi across the Peninsula and Frankston.
description: Same-day parcel delivery by taxi on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston. Documents, keys and small parcels taken directly to the door.

content.p: Sometimes something needs to get across town today, not in a few days. A signed contract, a set of spare keys, forgotten medication, a laptop left at the office or a small parcel that cannot wait for the post. Taxi Peninsula can carry it for you by taxi, going directly from pick-up to drop-off across the Mornington Peninsula, Frankston and further into Melbourne when needed.
Our parcel service is for items that fit comfortably in a sedan and can be carried safely by one person. Typical deliveries include:

ul: Documents and contracts that need to arrive the same day
House, car or business keys
A small parcel, gift or online order going to a relative
Items left behind after a visit, such as a phone charger, glasses or a bag
Supplies for a business that has run short during the day

content.p: We cannot carry anything illegal, dangerous or hazardous, and we may decline items that are too large, fragile or valuable to transport safely by taxi. Food and medication are best discussed with us first so we can confirm whether the trip is suitable. If you are unsure whether something qualifies, ask before you book.

The process is simple. Book the trip as you would a normal taxi, giving the pick-up address, the delivery address and a note explaining that it is a parcel only, with no passenger travelling. Include the names and phone numbers of the person handing the item over and the person receiving it, so the driver can call if needed. If the pick-up is from a business, mention which counter or office the item will be waiting at. The driver collects the item, goes directly to the destination and hands it over at the door.

Because the item travels in one vehicle from start to finish, there is no depot, no sorting and no change of hands along the way. That makes taxi delivery useful when timing matters, or when you would simply prefer that your item goes straight there.

content.h2: Getting things ready for the driver

content.p: A little preparation helps the delivery go smoothly. Package the item securely in an envelope, bag or box, and label it clearly with the recipient’s name and address. If the item is going to a business, check that someone will be there to receive it, particularly late in the day or near closing time. For deliveries to a home, let the recipient know it is on the way. If nobody will be available, tell us beforehand so we can agree what should happen.

Please do not send cash or irreplaceable valuables. For anything of significant value, consider whether you or someone you trust should travel with it instead, which you can do by booking a normal taxi trip. The same applies to anything that needs careful handling, such as artwork or delicate equipment, where it is better to have the owner present for the journey.

We run 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so a delivery can be booked for early in the morning, during business hours or late at night. If timing matters, tell us the deadline when you book, for example a document that must reach an office before it closes, so we can plan the pick-up accordingly. Common runs include Frankston to Mornington, Hastings to Rosebud, or anywhere on the Peninsula to a business in south-east Melbourne. We can also deliver further afield in Melbourne on request.

Deliveries are charged as a taxi trip from the pick-up to the delivery address. The online booking form shows a fare estimate before you confirm, and fixed quotes are available on request, which suits businesses that need the same delivery regularly. Local businesses such as real estate agents, accountants, pharmacies and trades sometimes use taxi delivery when a courier cannot get there in time, and households use it for urgent family errands. You can book a delivery online in about two minutes or by phone, and an SMS or email confirms the job.

expect: Direct same-day delivery, with no depot or sorting
Driver hands the item over at the door
Available 24/7 across the Peninsula and Frankston
Fare estimate shown before you confirm

faq.q: What sort of items can you deliver by taxi?
faq.a: We deliver documents, keys, small parcels and everyday items that fit comfortably in a sedan and can be carried by one person. We cannot carry anything illegal, dangerous or hazardous, and we may decline items that are too large, fragile or valuable. If you are unsure, ask us before booking.

faq.q: Does someone need to be there to receive the delivery?
faq.a: Yes, ideally. Our driver hands the item over at the door, so let the recipient know it is coming and include their name and phone number in the booking. If nobody will be home or the business may be closed, tell us beforehand so we can agree what to do.

faq.q: How is a parcel delivery priced?
faq.a: A delivery is charged as a taxi trip from the pick-up address to the delivery address. The booking form shows a fare estimate before you confirm, so you know roughly what to expect. Businesses that send items regularly can ask for a fixed quote for a particular run.

faq.q: Can you deliver outside the Peninsula?
faq.a: Yes. Most of our deliveries are local, between towns on the Mornington Peninsula and Frankston, but we travel anywhere in Melbourne. A document can go from Mornington to an office in the city, or keys from Rosebud to a family member in the south-east suburbs. Book it the same way as a local trip.

faq.q: Can I send something late at night?
faq.a: Yes. We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so deliveries can be booked outside business hours, such as keys for someone locked out or medication left behind after a visit. Make sure someone is available to receive the item at the other end, and add their contact details to the booking.

title: Pet transport
excerpt: Taxi trips for pets in carriers: vet visits, groomers and boarding, with the owner along or by arrangement.
description: Pet taxi on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston for vet visits, grooming and boarding. Pets travel in a secure carrier, with the owner along.

content.p: Getting a pet to the vet is not always easy, especially if you do not drive, are unwell yourself, or have a cat that objects loudly to every journey. Taxi Peninsula can take you and your pet to the vet, the groomer or a boarding kennel or cattery, across the Mornington Peninsula, Frankston and beyond. The key rule is simple: pets travel in a secure carrier, and in most cases the owner travels too.

A carrier keeps your pet safe and calm, and keeps the vehicle clean and comfortable for the passengers who travel after you, some of whom may have allergies. An animal loose in a moving car can be injured by a sudden stop, and a frightened pet may try to hide under a seat or jump out when the door opens. A sturdy carrier with a secure latch prevents all of that. Here are a few tips:

ul: Choose a carrier your pet can stand and turn around in, with good ventilation
Line it with a towel or absorbent pad in case of accidents
Bring a lead for dogs, so you can walk them in and out at each end
Have your pet’s paperwork, medication and vet details with you
Tell us the size of the carrier when you book so it fits comfortably

content.p: Larger dogs that do not fit in a standard carrier need to be discussed with us before booking. Let us know the breed and size, and we will tell you whether we can help with a suitable vehicle and arrangement.

content.h2: Vet visits and other common trips

content.p: Most pet trips are to a local vet clinic for check-ups, vaccinations, surgery or follow-up appointments. Others are to groomers, to boarding kennels and catteries before a holiday, or to collect a new pet from a breeder or shelter. Older pet owners who no longer drive often find a taxi is the only practical way to keep up regular check-ups for an ageing cat or dog. Because we run 24 hours a day, seven days a week, we can also take you to an after-hours emergency vet if your pet becomes unwell at night. Call us, explain the situation, and we will do what we can to get a vehicle to you.
For appointments where your pet is staying in, such as surgery or a procedure, book a one-way trip in, then book the trip home once the clinic tells you when your pet is ready to be collected.

content.h2: Can my pet travel without me?

content.p: Usually the owner travels with the pet, which is the simplest and calmest option for everyone. In some situations, such as a vet discharge while you are at work, unattended travel may be possible by arrangement. This needs to be discussed with us before booking, and we will need clear contact details at both ends, confirmation that someone will hand the pet over and someone will receive it, and the pet secured in its carrier. We may not be able to accept every request.

Assistance animals, such as guide dogs and other trained support dogs, are not pets and travel with their handler as normal. They do not need a carrier. If you travel with an assistance animal and use a wheelchair, our accessible vehicles have room for both, so mention it when you book.

When you book, choose a sedan or, if you are a wheelchair user, our ramp van or Maxi WAT, and add a note that a pet is travelling, with the type of animal and carrier size. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and confirmation arrives by SMS or email. Booking ahead is recommended, particularly for early appointments. If your pet tends to get anxious or carsick, a light meal well before the trip and a familiar blanket in the carrier can help, and our drivers will keep the ride smooth and the cabin cool. Let us know if the animal is unwell or recovering from surgery so the driver can take extra care at each end.

faq.q: Does my pet have to be in a carrier?
faq.a: Yes. Pets need to travel in a secure, well-ventilated carrier, which keeps them safe if the vehicle has to stop suddenly and keeps the car clean for other passengers. Assistance animals travelling with their handler are the exception. If your dog is too large for a carrier, talk to us before booking.

faq.q: Can you take my pet to the vet without me?
faq.a: Usually the owner travels with the pet. Unattended trips, such as collecting a pet after surgery, may be possible by arrangement, but they must be discussed with us before booking. We need contact details at both ends and confirmation that someone will hand over and receive the pet in its carrier.

faq.q: Can you take us to an emergency vet at night?
faq.a: We run 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so we can take you and your pet to an after-hours emergency vet. Phone us, explain the situation and give the clinic address, and we will do our best to get a vehicle to you. Have your pet ready in its carrier.

faq.q: I use a wheelchair. Can my pet travel with me?
faq.a: Yes. Book our wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT, and add a note that a pet is travelling, with the carrier size. Your wheelchair is secured with four-point restraints and the carrier is placed safely in the vehicle. Assistance animals travel with their handler as usual and do not need a carrier.

faq.q: What details should I give when booking a pet trip?
faq.a: Tell us the type of animal, the size of the carrier, the pick-up and destination addresses and whether you are travelling with your pet. For vet visits, include your appointment time. If the pet is travelling without you by arrangement, give the names and phone numbers of the people handing over and receiving it.
